# EXPERIENCED CONSTRUCTION PROFESSIONAL

Brad is a highly skilled Mechanical Mining and Minerals professional with over 25 years of experience across the mining construction industry, fixed plant maintenance, and the automotive sector—spanning both Brownfield and Greenfield operations throughout Australia. He brings extensive expertise in managing complex processing facilities through all project phases, from construction and commissioning to operational handover.

Brad has a proven track record of successfully leading large-scale industrial processing and infrastructure projects, underpinned by a strong understanding of the WHS Mines Regulations & Act. He is also highly experienced in client and contractor engagement, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality project delivery.

Most recently, Brad served as the site-based Construction Manager for Calibre/WSP, leading the Rio Tinto/Calibre Integrated Project Team (IPT) on the $+ \$ 500$ million West Angelas A West Project (WAAW).

Prior to this, he worked with HATCH as a Construction Superintendent on the Kemerton Expansion Project and was previously appointed Deputy Construction Manager on Rio Tinto’s $\$ 6.55$ billion Robe Valley Sustaining Project (RVS).

Earlier, Brad served as Construction Superintendent at Newmont’s Tanami Gold Mine in the Northern Territory. He played a key role in the successful delivery and commissioning of a major plant expansion, including the installation of a new secondary ball mill and associated infrastructure. He also oversaw the construction and commissioning of two gas-fired power stations with a combined output of 101.5 MW, connected via $4 2 k m$ of 66kV overhead power lines.

A highly motivated and determined leader, Brad consistently demonstrates initiative, professionalism, and the drive to deliver successful outcomes across all aspects of a project.

# Project Snapshot:

West Angelas A West (WAAW)

The West Angelas A West (WAAW) Project is designed to sustain the current mine production capacity at 35 Mtpa, with ramp-up scheduled from 2026. The project encompasses the development of three new pits: A West 1 (AW1), A West 2 (AW2), and A West 3 (AW3). The goal is to initiate mining activities at AW1 by Q1 2025 and at AW3 by Q4 2025. Located between the existing West Angelas Deposit A and Deposit D, WAAW will link the infrastructure between Hub A and Hub CD and provide critical mining resources to extend the mine life.

# Project Snapshot:

Kemerton Expansion Project (KEP)

Kemerton Expansion Project (KEP) is a joint venture construction team comprising of both Albemarle (Owner) and Hatch (EPCM). This team will deliver all Construction and Commissioning including handovers to the Owner Albermarle of processing Trains 3 & 4 including all associated NPI works. Trains 3 & 4 are essentially a mirror image of the first 2 trains and will double the current plant throughput capacity. Operating at full capacity, the Kemerton plant is designed to produce up to 100 ktpa.
